text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Manchester United and Brighton & Hove Albion at Old Trafford!
Following the recent international period, Manchester United return to Premier League duty aiming to continue their flawless home record so far.
While the Red Devils have posted two wins at Old Trafford, they have lost both away fixtures, including at Arsenal, who beat United 3-1 in London two weeks ago.
For all the off-field turmoil undermining their cause, manager Erik ten Hag will send his side out today having gone unbeaten through their last 32 home matches in all competitions.

Brighton secured a 2-1 victory at Old Trafford on the opening weekend of last season, and they have started this term in even more impressive style: having won three of their first four matches and scored 12 goals in the process, Albion are among the early Premier League front-runners.

The Seagulls signed off for the international break with a 3-1 home victory over Newcastle United, in which Republic of Ireland striker Evan Ferguson netted his first top-flight hat-trick, and Roberto De Zerbi is now preparing his team for a first European campaign.

Manchester United make three changes to the team that started against Arsenal last time out, as McTominay is brought in from the cold following another impressive spell with Scotland, Hojlund is offered his first start and Reguilon makes his debut.
Antony and Jadon Sancho are both unavailable for selection, while Varane, Mount and Amrabat are among several players sidelined by injury.
Ahead of next week's Europa League game against AEK Athens, De Zerbi rotates his squad today, making six changes to the Brighton XI that overcame Newcastle United.
While Adingra, Dahoud and ex-Man United striker Welbeck are among those introduced, Fati starts on the bench.
Despite his hat-trick heroics last time out, Ferguson is also named among the substitutes, having missed the recent Euro 2024 qualifiers due to injury.
The players are out on the pitch at Old Trafford, and kick-off is now just moments away!
Brighton kick off, and we are under way in Manchester!
Determined play from Reguilon in midfield recovers the ball, and his forward run towards the left byline then earns Manchester United the first corner of the game.
However, having taken it short, they almost immediately lose possession.
A foul on Dalot near the touchline sees Lamptey pick up an early yellow card, and the Brighton full-back will have to tread carefully from now on.

SAVE! Steele sticks out a leg to deny Rashford at the near post! After a direct run from the Man United forward, he reaches the byline and eludes Veltman's challenge; however, his close-range shot lacks conviction and allows Brighton's goalkeeper to make the save.
Following a free-kick routine orchestrated by Fernandes, a looping header from the edge of the box by Hojlund sails well over the crossbar.
It's been an impressive start from the home side so far.
Rashford slings over a dangerous low cross fron the left touchline, which Hojlund only narrowly fails to make contact with, as he dives desperately into the six-yard box trying to make contact.
Dunk dives in to make a vital block inside his own box, after Reguilon plays in Rashford, who takes a couple of touches then unleashes a powerful strike at goal from the left-hand side of the area.
Ultimately, it wouldn't have counted anyway, as the flag goes up for offside soon afterwards.

Alleviating the early pressure from their hosts, Brighton mount a quick counter: Solly sends Mitoma away on the break, but when the latter finds Lallana just outside the Manchester United box, a heavy touch sees the move disintegrate.

Heading into today's game, Manchester United had won each of their last eight Premier League matches at Old Trafford; they last enjoyed a longer home winning run in the competition back in 2013, en route to winning their last league title under Sir Alex Ferguson.
After Lamptey progresses up the left flank, Martinez is forced into a hurried hack away from danger as Welbeck closes him down tigerishly inside Man United's area.
Having been pinned back for much of the first 10 minutes, Brighton have since grown in confidence and are getting into their familiar passing rhythm.

BRIGHTON LEAD! Hitting his old club where it hurts, Welbeck slots home a 10-yard finish from the centre of the area, following Adingra's low cross from the right! He stays cool to steer the ball into the net, leaving Onana well beaten and putting Brighton 1-0 ahead at Old Trafford!
Pulling the ball back across the box from near the right byline, Adingra sets up Welbeck for the game's opening goal.
With his first goal of the 2023-24 season, Welbeck has now scored four times in 12 Premier League appearances against Manchester United since leaving his boyhood club.
Much to his apparent dismay, Van Hecke is booked by the referee for engaging in some time-wasting along with Brighton goalkeeper Steele.
After Dalot skips away from Mitoma on the right, his cutback is then hammered towards the target by Rashford, who sees the ball bounce back off the well-placed Dahoud.
That was a decent half-chance for the England striker.
Brighton are bossing the ball at the moment, as the nervous energy builds inside Old Trafford.
Manchester United's recent woes have not extended to home turf, but they find themselves behind again, heading towards half-time.
It's still the visitors in charge at the Theatre of Dreams, as Albion effortlessly stroke the ball about and their hosts chase shadows.
This is how Brighton prefer to protect a lead.
Picking the ball up from Lallana midway through Man United's half, Welbeck takes a few short strides before letting fly with a 25-yard effort that rises comfortably over the crossbar.

OFF THE POST! Rashford comes close again! A driving run inside from the left leaves Van Hecke helplessly back-tracking, and the forward's shot is deflected onto the goalframe by Veltman's attempted block!
After some superb control by Lamptey opens up a few yards of space, Dalot shuts down Mitoma's sprint down the left touchline and United ultimately get the ball away to safety.
Old Trafford has gone very quiet now, as Brighton dictate the tempo of this game and seem to have endless time on the ball.
The Seagulls passing has been so crisp since taking the lead earlier on.
Sprinting back into place, Reguilon uses his pace to avert danger, as Welbeck almost breaks free in the area and lines up a shot at goal.
GOAL FOR UNITED? Seemingly scoring his first Manchester United goal, Hojlund turns the ball home from close range after excellent work by Rashford on the left flank.
The latter twice skins Van Hecke and then delivers an accurate low cross - but did he carry the ball over the byline? The VAR will decide!
NO GOAL! The VAR intervenes: Brighton keep their lead! Rashford had taken the ball just over the left byline before teeing up Hojlund's 'goal', which is now ruled out as a result.
Steele and his defenders play a risky game in developing play from the back, and the goalkeeper is a whisker away from giving the ball to Hojlund before quickly averting calamity.

MISS! Once again, Rashford drifts in from the left and sets up a shot at goal, but his attempt is skewed narrowly wide of the right-hand post! He's created plenty of openings during the first half, but not quite been able to finish it all off.
A frustrated, rather reckless lunge from behind on Dahoud results in a booking for Bruno Fernandes.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-1 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION
Rewarded for their bravery and control of possession at Old Trafford, Brighton lead at the break, thanks to a goal from ex-Manchester United man Welbeck.
While Rashford provided a constant threat with runs from out to in, United have failed to find a way past Steele so far, with Hojlund having a goal ruled out by the VAR on his full debut.
The outcome of an entertaining encounter remains very much in the balance, but it is De Zerbi's side who have an advantage to defend during the second half.
Brighton are unbeaten in their last 25 Premier League matches when leading at half-time, recording no less than 21 wins in the process.
The Seagulls have also won all three times they have led at the break this term.
Manchester United did come back from two goals down to beat Nottingham Forest earlier this season, though.
The hosts kick off, and we are back under way in Manchester!
Dalot steals the ball from Mitoma and springs a quick counter-attack: after Fernandes finds Rashford on the left, though, the latter's cutback from the byline cannot find another red jersey.
Having had to suffer without the ball for sustained spells during the first half, Manchester United are now neatly keeping possession, as they aim to find a route back into this game.

WIDE! Another wayward finish by Rashford hits the side-netting! Veltman and Van Hecke just cannot cope with his driving runs inside from the left flank, but it was a weak attempt from a promising position, with Hojlund also waiting in the centre.

THE SEAGULLS STRIKE AGAIN! Brighton extend their advantage, as Mitoma and Lamptey combine on the left side of the area, before the latter's pass picks out Gross, who steers the ball into the net from near the penalty spot! It was not great defending from the hosts, but the away fans don't care: 2-0 to Brighton!

events.action: steers the ball into the net

text: After receiving the ball from Mitoma on the left side of the box, Lamptey's scuffed pass to Gross provides the assist for Brighton's second goal.
Defeat to Brighton today would see Manchester United suffer as many as three defeats in their first five matches of a league campaign for the first time since 1989-90, under Sir Alex Ferguson.
Steele fields the ball in the centre of his goal, dropping down to smother a shot from Fernandes, who tries his luck from outside the area.
Rashford this time drives a shot at goal from the edge of the area, which is heavily deflected behind for a corner-kick.
However, the hosts can make nothing of the subsequent set-piece situation.
With a more comfortable cushion between them and their hosts, Brighton are now back in control of the ball.
It's a long way back for Man United now.
A driving run and cross by Dalot wins United another corner, but once again they fail to make the most of a set-piece opportunity.
De Zerbi turns to the bench for fresh legs: the vastly experienced Lallana makes way, with young Barcelona loanee Ansu Fati sent on to replace him.
Opening goalscorer Welbeck is also withdrawn; Joao Pedro will be his replacement up front.
The home side also make a couple of changes: first, Mejbri comes on for Casemiro.
Making his 200th Premier League appearance, Martial is also introduced by Ten Hag, who hauls off Hojlund.
Rashford's latest attempt sails straight into the waiting gloves of Steele, who comfortably repels the United striker's dipping 20-yard free-kick.
Brighton have won their last three league matches against Manchester United - as many as in their first 17 - and they are now less than half an hour from extending that winning run to four games.
But can they hold on?
Eriksen delivers a driven corner from the left, but Dunk's intervention clears the ball away for a throw-in.
Eventually, Brighton play their way out of trouble, and they keep possession while the clock ticks down.

BRIGHTON BAG A THIRD! The visitors lead 3-0 at Old Trafford! Piling more misery on Man United, Joao Pedro expertly converts Lamptey's pass from just inside the box, steering the ball past Onana's despairing dive with a precise side-foot finish! What a scoreline we have here!
Another assist for Lamptey: he passes the ball into Joao Pedro's path and watches on as the ball then nestles into the back of the net.

UNITED BACK IN IT! The hosts reduce their arrears, as Hannibal receives the ball from Martinez and slams home a superb strike from just outside the area, finding the bottom-right corner! It's suddenly 3-1 to Brighton, but there's still plenty of work left to do for Ten Hag's men!
Martinez picks out Hannibal with a pass leading to Manchester United's first goal of the game.
A rugged challenge by Veltman sends Reguilon sprawling and concedes a corner-kick.
Following the set-piece, Fernandes chips a ball back into the box from the right, before Lindelof heads the ball over the crossbar under pressure.
Having set up two goals today, Lamptey is now withdrawn; former Liverpool, Leeds United and Manchester City man Milner comes on to a 'warm' welcome from the Old Trafford faithful.
De Zerbi also replaces Dahoud, with Gilmour taking his place in central midfield.
SAVE! Closing down the angle at his near post, Onana keeps out a prodded shot from close range by Mitoma, who seemed set to score Brighton's fourth goal when set free by Joao Pedro's throughball.
Brighton are patiently keeping possession at the back, as they consistently evade United's disjointed press.
It's hard to envisage how the home side can get anything from this game now, as they can barely get hold of the ball.
A brief spell of pressure comes to an abrupt end when Dalot fouls Mitoma deep inside Brighton territory.
It's been quite a duel between the two of them today, and no quarter has been given.
Ten Hag goes for broke with a triple substitution: first, Reguilon is replaced by Garnacho.
Wan-Bissaka is thrown on in place of Martinez.
Finally, McTominay makes way as Pellistri is offered a brief cameo in testing circumstances.
Brighton also make their final change, with Ferguson returning from injury to replace Adingra for the final few minutes.
SAVE! Once again, Joao Pedro drops deep to feed in an attacking colleague, as he picks out Ferguson's run into the box from the right.
The teenage substitute then drives a low shot at Onana, who makes a sharp save!
Ansu Fati tries his luck with a shot from the centre of the area, which is saved comfortably enough by Onana in the bottom-right corner.
Again, it was Joao Pedro who played the final pass.
Six minutes of stoppage time have been indicated by the match officials, but if anything it seems more likely that Brighton will score again than Manchester United can stage a dramatic late comeback.
For lunging into a challenge on Ferguson, Hannibal is shown a yellow card by the referee.

SUPER STOP! Onana prevents the hosts' embarrassment becoming more acute, as he dives low to his left in order to keep out Ansu Fati's goalbound strike! Gilmour sent the young loanee through, and he really should have scored!
Fernandes cuts inside and delivers a slightly aimless cross, and Veltman responds by stepping in and diverting it away to safety.
Brighton are seeing this game out quite comfortably.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-3 BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION

Continuing their unprecedented dominance over Manchester United, a slick and clinical Brighton side post their fourth straight win over the Red Devils - and their two-goal winning margin could well have been bigger.
Ex-United striker Welbeck set them on their way, and Joao Pedro's second-half strike capped another fine performance from De Zerbi's men.
A disjointed display from the hosts saw them greeted by many empty seats and some booing at the final whistle, while the Seagulls will fly home with 12 Premier League points on the board already.

It does not get any easier for Manchester United in their next outing, as they tackle Bayern Munich in Bavaria, before they return to Premier League duty much closer to home, meeting Burnley at Turf Moor.
Brighton, meanwhile, host AEK Athens in Thursday's Europa League debut, then Bournemouth await next weekend.
That's all from Old Trafford today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
